newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open off 0.40 to 0.80 cent.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open off 0.40 to 0.80 cent.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open slightly weaker Monday as LME tested the low of $2,250 per tonne overnight but held this level so far.
LME reported Monday that stocks fell 1,775 tonnes to 157,900 tonnes.
COMEX stocks fell 185 short tons Friday to 42,562 short tons.
COMEX May copper was called 0.40 to 0.80 cent weaker from Friday's close of 106.50 cents a lb. May traded from 106.70 to 105.15 cents on ACCESS.
CFTC's Commitments of Traders report released late Friday showed a decline in speculative long positions in the week ended April 8, and a decline in commercial short positions.
Speculators held 10,701 long positions and 3,000 short positions, compared to 13,872 and 2,790, respectively, in the previous week.
Commercials held 17,701 long positions and 31,367 short positions in week ended April 8, compared to 17,834 and 38,406 respectively in the previous week.
Nonreportable positions remain significant, with 21,679 long and 15,714 short in week ended April 8.
No major economic data are due Monday as the financial markets awaited nervously the consumer price index Tuesday.
